title: Traffic spike on a stateless API
story: 60 users (1 s think time) flood one web replica capped at 0.5 CPU (about 25 req/s). Expected heal: scale out.

timeline.thought: Dry run passes with no guardrail violations (total CPU stays at 2×0.5=1.0, within max_cpus; total memory 2×128m=256m, well under max_total_memory 768m).

args.summary: Scaled web from 1 to 2 replicas to relieve CPU saturation causing latency spikes (stateless service, traefik load-balances automatically).

timeline.note: waiting for the median of 5 probes < 500 ms (≤ 60 s; an improvement is never rolled back)

timeline.thought:
ROOT CAUSE: CPU saturation on the single `web` replica — probe p50 jumped from ~23-54ms baseline to 1336-1558ms (threshold 800ms, one hard timeout at 1800ms) right as `cpu_pct_peak_total` hit 52.0% against the per-replica limit of 50% (`cpu_limit_pct_per_replica: 50`), with memory nowhere near its cap (20.8MB/128MB, no OOM, exit_code 0). The BrokenPipeError in logs is a client disconnecting after the request stalled, a symptom of the latency not its cause.
CHANGE: Scaled `web` from 1 → 2 replicas (cpus/memory unchanged at 0.5/128m each); traefik load-balances across replicas automatically for this stateless service, halving CPU-bound load per instance.
GUARDRAILS: Within limits — replicas 2 ≤ max_replicas 3; total cpus 2×0.5=1.0 = max_cpus 1.0 (not exceeded); total memory 2×128m=256m ≪ max_total_memory 768m; action type "scale" is in allowed_actions; dry-run reported no violations.
FOLLOW-UP: Watch next few probe cycles — if peak CPU still approaches saturation under load, consider raising max_cpus or further scaling (within device's 4 CPUs/4GiB), and investigate whether request handling can be made less CPU-heavy per request (~20ms CPU/request) to improve headroom.
